active.status_check: Official WOWII all.html still marks 19 as O (local dump 2026-09-12). Follows from #13 when avg ecc ≤ diam−1. Remaining case is nearly self-centered graphs.
active.why_tractable: Finite connected graphs; invariants computable; only self-centered graphs can beat #13.
active.main_risk: May be a short corollary of proved #13 and #16; proving those from the literature is out of scope. A genuine counterexample would have to violate the published #16 bound as well.

active.status_check: Official WOWII all.html marks 61 as O. No public Lean counterexample repo found on 2026-09-12.
active.why_tractable: Need residue close to the induced-forest number and diameter ≥ 4. Residue and forest number are computable on small n.
active.main_risk: residue ≤ α ≤ f is classical, so a counterexample needs a large diameter gap rather than a small-n random graph.

active.status_check: Official WOWII all.html marks 133 as O. Lean path is largest induced path order, matching the WOWII path number.
active.why_tractable: If G has a 4-cycle then a geodesic from a centre already gives path ≥ rad+1, so the inequality holds. Only C4-free graphs remain.
active.main_risk: C4-free diameter-2 graphs of large degree (Moore / polarity) may be the only dangerous class and may still have long induced paths.

standby.note: DeLaVina notes f ≥ b/2+1, so the p=1 case is easy. Need large path cover. Stars give equality, not a counterexample.

Lean uses degreeL2Norm of the complement. WOWII 49's path-on-38 counterexample confirms that length(·) in these entries is the complement length. The no-overline HTML reading is a loophole, not the intended statement.
